officials.address: 33000 Civic Center Drive Livonia, MI 48154
officials.bio: Brandon McCullough grew up in Livonia, attending Cleveland, Emerson, and Franklin schools. He holds a degree in Construction Engineering from Lawrence Technological University and has a professional background in facilities management and construction, including work with Habitat for Humanity. He is married to Kacie, a teacher at Franklin High School, and they have a daughter, Harper.

officials.name: Carrie Budzinski
officials.address: 33000 Civic Center Drive Livonia, MI 48154
officials.bio: Carrie Budzinski, a lifelong Livonia resident, was elected City Councilmember in 2024. She has a background in marketing and public service, having worked for the U.S. Senate and various non-profits. Passionate about her community, she has served on the Livonia Historical and Library Commissions and founded Vote. Run. Serve.

officials.name: Eileen McDonnell
officials.address: 33000 Civic Center Drive Livonia, MI 48154
officials.bio: Eileen McDonnell has been a Livonia resident for 30 years, with children attending Livonia Public Schools and two grandchildren who enjoy the city's parks. She brings five years of experience as a Livonia Public Schools Trustee, where she applied her contract management expertise to a $195 million school improvement bond initiative. She looks forward to working with citizens, council, and administration to enhance Livonia's close-knit, small-town atmosphere.

officials.name: Martha Ptashnik
officials.address: 33000 Civic Center Drive Livonia, MI 48154
officials.bio: Martha grew up in Livonia and, with her husband Brian, chose to raise their two children there. She is a teacher for Livonia Public Schools, currently serving as mathematics department chairman at Livonia Churchill High School. Her background includes experience as a retail buyer, giving her a unique perspective on the city's challenges.

officials.name: Robin Persiconi
officials.address: 33000 Civic Center Drive Livonia, MI 48154
officials.bio: The daughter of immigrant parents, Robin Persiconi learned early the values of hard work, integrity, and giving back to the community, starting work at her father's small business at 15. After law school, she founded The Law Office of Robin Persiconi, building a respected legal practice over 23 years. She continues her law practice while raising two daughters with her husband and is active in her Rotary Club and other service organizations.

officials.name: Kayleigh Reid
officials.address: 33000 Civic Center Drive Livonia, MI 48154
officials.bio: Kayleigh Reid grew up in Livonia and is married with three boys. She is the Executive Director of the Livonia Spree and previously worked at Lawrence Tech University for ten years in the President and Provost's office.

officials.name: Patrick Brockway
officials.address: 33000 Civic Center Drive Livonia, MI 48154
officials.bio: Patrick brings extensive experience in public service as a management analyst with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, applying data-driven analysis and strategic problem-solving. He previously served in various roles with the Department of Homeland Security-Transportation Security Administration as an officer, supervisor, and training instructor.

officials.bio: Kenneth D. Johnson was elected the 67th mayor of the magnificent City of Muskegon in the great State of Michigan on November 2, 2021. He was sworn into office on January 3, 2022. His current term runs through the end of 2029.

officials.name: Rebecca St. Clair
officials.address:
933 Terrace St.
Muskegon, MI 49440
officials.bio: Rebecca St Clair is a Commissioner at-Large for the City of Muskegon, having moved there in 2002. She is passionate about her city and believes in collaborative governance that benefits all residents, ensuring everyone has a voice. Her priorities include listening to constituents, being a good steward of public funds, and promoting equity, justice, and inclusion.

officials.name: Austin
officials.bio: Councilman-at-Large Adrian Austin is a lifelong resident of Pontiac, Michigan, committed to serving his community with integrity, transparency, and innovative solutions. Professionally, he has distinguished himself as a two-term UAW Chairperson and Bargaining Representative, advocating for workers' rights and negotiating significant gains. Beyond his professional and political service, he is a founder of Operation Pontiac Pride, a community organization, and continues to lead with vision and dedication to Pontiac's citizens.

officials.name: Campbell
officials.bio: Regina K. Campbell is the City Councilwoman for Pontiac’s District 6, committed to building trust through collaboration and advancing policies that strengthen neighborhoods, support local businesses, and promote equitable and sustainable growth. She brings over a decade of experience in construction, real estate, and community development, and is the founder of Ginasis Construction. Councilperson Campbell is deeply engaged in the community through volunteer service, youth mentorship, housing advocacy, and voting-rights initiatives.

officials.name: Carrington
officials.bio: Councilman William A. Carrington is a proven servant leader whose work is rooted in integrity, collaboration, and measurable results, deeply committed to strengthening Pontiac’s neighborhoods and improving the quality of life for all residents. Born in Knoxville, Tennessee, and raised in Flint, Michigan, he holds multiple degrees and serves as Data and Quality Manager for Wayne State University’s School of Medicine and an Adjunct Professor.

officials.name: Goodman
officials.address: 47450 Woodward Avenue, Pontiac, Michigan 48342
officials.bio: Mikal Goodman is a lifelong Pontiac resident who grew up on the city's East Side. Since taking office in 2021, he has made housing justice his top priority, leading efforts to hold slumlords accountable and protect families from exploitation, and securing funds for homelessness prevention.

officials.name: Jackson
officials.bio: Chris serves as the Director of Policy and Innovation for Honor Community Health and was previously the Executive Director for the Michigan Legislative Black Caucus. He is also an advocate in the Cannabis Industry, serving as Chairman of the Board for the National Cannabis Industry Association, and is the Team Market Owner of the Pontiac Pharaohs basketball team. Councilperson Jackson was elected to represent City Council District One in November 2025 to a four-year term expiring on January 1, 2030.

officials.name: James
officials.bio: Kathalee James retired from General Motors as a Senior Quality Engineer and holds a Bachelor of Arts degree from Oakland University. She was elected to represent City Council District Four in November 2025 to a four-year term expiring on January 1, 2030. She has affiliations with Eastside Church of God and was the Founder and President of Friends of the Pontiac Parks Association.

officials.name: Jones
officials.bio: Councilwoman Milanna Jones is a dynamic and self-driven woman who has called Pontiac her home since 2017. Since moving to Pontiac, she has remained an active member in her community. Her mission has been to provide thoughtful and impactful leadership in her community and allocate her time and energy efficiently for the well-being and longevity of her community.

officials.name: Mayor McGuinness
officials.address: 47450 Woodward Avenue, Pontiac, Michigan 48342
officials.bio: Happy 2026, Pontiac! It is my great honor to work for you as our municipality's Chief Executive Officer. We have a hardworking and dedicated team here at Pontiac City Hall. I'm grateful for the opportunity to work alongside them as we deliver results for Pontiac residents.

officials.name: Bill Ostash
officials.bio: Councilman Bill Ostash is a lifelong resident of the Great Lakes Bay Region, holding a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science with a minor in Management. He has served on the City Council since 2018 and was previously active in historic preservation, including chairing the Saginaw Historic District Commission. He is dedicated to Saginaw's progress and rebirth.

officials.bio: Eric D. Braddock, Sr. was born in Saginaw, Michigan, and served honorably in the United States Army before pursuing higher education. Upon returning to Saginaw, he dedicated himself to public service, community advocacy, and education, including roles with Saginaw Citizens United for Equity and Justice and the Saginaw Public School District. He was elected as a Saginaw City Councilman in 2024, continuing his mission to serve his hometown.

officials.name: Heidi G. Wiggins
officials.address: 1315 South Washington Avenue Saginaw, MI 48601
officials.bio: Council Member Heidi Wiggins is a lifelong resident of Saginaw and a graduate of Delta College. She began serving on City Council in 2024 and is committed to ensuring all City of Saginaw residents are represented and have the best environment to live, grow, and prosper.

officials.name: Michael Balls
officials.address: 1315 South Washington Avenue Saginaw, MI 48601
officials.bio: Councilman Michael Balls is a lifelong resident of Saginaw, dedicated to the common good. He retired from Saginaw Steering GM in 2007 and currently works at Nexteer Corporation. Having served on the City Council since 2013, he is committed to building a stronger Saginaw.

officials.name: Tobias Young
officials.address: 1315 South Washington Avenue Saginaw, MI 48601
officials.bio: Tobias Young is a dedicated lifelong resident of Saginaw, serving as a Council Member since 2025. With a background as a journeyman electrician and entrepreneur, he brings practical experience and a deep commitment to community development, advocating for housing and small businesses. He is actively involved in his community and prides himself on a hands-on approach to problem-solving.

officials.name: Priscilla Garcia
officials.address: 1315 South Washington Avenue Saginaw, MI 48601
officials.bio: Mayor Pro Tem Priscilla Garcia is a lifelong Saginaw resident with a master's degree in business administration, dedicated to community service through various organizations. Elected to City Council in 2022 and Mayor Pro Tem in 2024, she works professionally as a Licensed Medicare Specialist and aims to ensure Saginaw's vibrancy for future generations.

officials.name: Brenda Moore
officials.address: 1315 South Washington Avenue Saginaw, MI 48601
officials.bio: Mayor Brenda Fay Moore is a life-long resident of the City of Saginaw and a proud graduate of Saginaw High School. Since her 2013 election to City Council, she has actively engaged with the Michigan Municipal League, serving as President of the Michigan Black Caucus of Local Elected Officials and the Michigan Association of Mayors. Elected Mayor in 2020, she aims to positively impact youth and young adults and serves on several influential boards and commissions.
